main.title: Mario Kart Tour
main.summary: Mario Kart Tour was a 2019 kart racing game developed and published by Nintendo for Android and iOS.

cards.heading: Mario Kart on mobile devices
cards.text: Mario Kart Tour was a 2019 kart racing game developed and published by Nintendo for Android and iOS. The game featured biweekly, downloadable themed tours with different cups, each of which had three courses and a bonus challenge. Courses were based on those that have appeared previously in the Mario Kart series, as well as new ones that are based on real-world cities.

cards.heading: From launch to the end of service
cards.text: Mario Kart Tour was announced in January 2018 and was released on September 25, 2019, on Apple's App Store and Google Play. The game received mixed reviews from critics, who praised its simple gameplay and controls but criticized its monetization and gacha elements as well as its lack of characters at launch. Reception improved over time following additional content releases and removal of the gacha elements. The game was shut down on September 29, 2026, at 11:00 p.m. Pacific Daylight Time.

main.title: Code Vein
main.subtitle: Surviving With a Shared Memory
main.summary: Code Vein is a 2019 action RPG about Revenants, blood and lost memories, with changeable Blood Codes and a companion in combat.

cards.heading: Revenants in a ruined world
cards.text: Code Vein is a 2019 action role-playing game developed by Bandai Namco Studios and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment. Revenants seek blood and recover memories in a ruined world. Players can change their combat role through Blood Codes and travel with an AI-controlled companion or another player.

cards.heading: Changing builds with Blood Codes
cards.text: Blood Codes provide different statistics and abilities. Switching between them allows the player to test another approach to an encounter without keeping a permanent starting class. Equipment, timing and the selected abilities all influence how a fight unfolds.

cards.heading: Fighting with a companion
cards.text: A companion can distract enemies, create openings and help the player survive. Combat still requires attention to attacks and positioning, but the ally gives opponents another target. Players can take advantage of that support when approaching a difficult encounter.

cards.heading: Vestiges preserve memories and Blood Codes
cards.text: The protagonist awakens within the ruined city of Gaol of the Mists, where they meet Io, a mysterious woman compelled to help them, and Louis Amamiya, a fellow Revenant and a researcher seeking to secure a steady supply of Blood Beads for the Gaol’s inhabitants. They make contact with the vestige of a Lost without becoming frenzied, acquiring its memories and Blood Code, an individual trait that grants each Revenant unique powers. Louis learns that the protagonist can use the Blood Code of whoever shares their blood.

main.title: Concrete Genie
main.subtitle: Bring a town back with paint
main.summary: Concrete Genie is Pixelopus's PlayStation 4 action-adventure, released on 8 October 2019. Ash uses a magical brush to paint living creatures across the walls of Denska, a neglected seaside town. His drawings supply companions and abilities that help him reach new areas and restore colour to the streets. The player builds scenes from collected designs, turning blank surfaces into small animated landscapes. The story connects that act of making something with Ash's experience of bullying, giving the town's recovery a personal purpose beyond opening another route.

cards.heading: Bring a town back with paint
cards.text: Concrete Genie is Pixelopus's PlayStation 4 action-adventure, released on 8 October 2019. Ash uses a magical brush to paint living creatures across the walls of Denska, a neglected seaside town. His drawings supply companions and abilities that help him reach new areas and restore colour to the streets. The player builds scenes from collected designs, turning blank surfaces into small animated landscapes. The story connects that act of making something with Ash's experience of bullying, giving the town's recovery a personal purpose beyond opening another route.

cards.heading: A creature’s colour becomes an ability
cards.text: Painted genies respond to Ash and can help solve obstacles around their walls. Different colours give them different powers, so choosing a creature becomes part of understanding what a location requires. Painting also asks the player to arrange the forms that make up each scene, making the wall visibly reflect those choices. The DualShock 4's motion controls support the movement of the brush. A puzzle and a drawing therefore share the same action: the player creates a companion whose ability can then change the way Ash moves through Denska.

cards.heading: Protect what has been made
cards.text: The bullies move through the town and can threaten Ash or damage his paintings, asking the player to judge when it is safe to work. Restoring a ruined wall lets the activity continue instead of making its loss permanent. New designs and areas gradually enlarge the collection of things that can be painted. Dominic Robilliard directed the project, with Samual Marshall supplying the score. Reviewers generally welcomed its visual character and creative interactions. It became Pixelopus's final released game before Sony closed the studio in 2023.

main.title: Disco Elysium
main.subtitle: A detective listens to his own skills
main.summary: Disco Elysium is ZA/UM?s 2019 detective RPG, built around dialogue, investigation and twenty-four skills that speak as inner voices.

cards.heading: An investigation led by dialogue
cards.text: Disco Elysium is a detective role-playing game released for PC on October 15, 2019. ZA/UM?s five-year development drew on thirteen years of earlier worldbuilding. Dialogue and investigation drive its encounters, while twenty-four skills interrupt with intuitions and advice. The Thought Cabinet lets ideas become part of the character?s abilities.

cards.heading: Twenty-four competing inner voices
cards.text: Logic, Empathy and the other skills influence how the detective reads a situation. They can notice a clue, suggest a response or lead him towards a questionable conclusion. Raising a skill makes its perspective more prominent, leaving the player to decide whether to follow its advice.

cards.heading: The consequences of failure
cards.text: A failed check can lead to an unexpected conversation or an embarrassing incident rather than ending the investigation. Mistakes still have consequences, but the story can continue through them. The detective?s weaknesses become part of the role the player creates.

cards.heading: Developing ideas in the Thought Cabinet
cards.text: The Thought Cabinet lets the detective internalise ideas encountered during the investigation. Each takes time and can change his abilities. Choosing what to develop, retain or forget adds another layer to character building.

cards.heading: Returning to Martinaise
cards.text: Martinaise concentrates characters, tasks and clues within a relatively compact district. New information can make a familiar street or locked door worth revisiting. Remembering the people and places already encountered helps connect the investigation.

cards.heading: A world developed over thirteen years
cards.text: ZA/UM had spent thirteen years developing the world before the game?s release. Revachol?s political history and wider geography emerge through local people, conversations and places. The district suggests conflicts that began before the detective arrived.

cards.heading: Politics in the detective?s conversations
cards.text: Political ideas enter conversations and some can be developed through the Thought Cabinet. The detective?s responses influence how other people see him, while irony and contradiction complicate his claims. His beliefs become another part of the role-playing alongside his practical skills.

features.title: The people between the dialogue branches
features.summary: Writers and performers reshape a conversation.

cards.heading: A conversation needs a working structure
cards.text: In a pre-release Rezzed interview, Robert Kurvitz describes organising Disco Elysium's branching dialogue through visual software. A conversation could grow into a complicated structure, and the project's eight-person writing team worked from a central synopsis while expanding its possibilities. The account shows an authoring problem behind selecting a line. Someone had to keep connections intelligible while making room for alternatives. A branching conversation was not simply a finished page divided by buttons; it was a structure that needed continued maintenance.

cards.heading: Writing what someone may never see
cards.text: Kurvitz also describes following small jokes and unlikely choices into consequences, despite the work they might create elsewhere. Some story moments would hold the main investigation together, while side cases could develop their own clues and reconnect with it. That balance meant writing material a particular player might never encounter. His comments are plans from before release, rather than a complete inventory of the finished game. They nevertheless reveal why a writer's task extends beyond producing a memorable sentence: a choice must remain meaningful after someone has selected it.

cards.heading: Another voice changes the reading
cards.text: Discussing The Final Cut in 2021, writer and narrative designer Justin Keenan describes the difference made by voice acting. Lenval Brown's narration brought a presence to inner voices; Keenan said the team began hearing that voice while writing. Animator Eduardo Rubio also worked to make encountered characters feel more alive. Text, performance and movement were changing together. This production history belongs beside the written words, because the same line can be understood differently depending on how a voice holds its pace and emphasis.

cards.heading: Returning to an unfinished intention
cards.text: Keenan also identifies player criticism that political alignments had felt insufficiently developed as stories. Political dream quests had been discussed earlier but cut before the original release; The Final Cut gave the team a chance to return to them. This was a conversation between an existing intention and what players reported experiencing. It did not require treating every request as an instruction. The work was to decide which criticism exposed a gap worth addressing, then write and build something that made those choices more substantial inside the game.

main.title: Ring Fit Adventure
main.subtitle: An adventure moved by exercise
main.summary: Ring Fit Adventure is Nintendo's exercise role-playing game, released for Switch on 18 October 2019.

cards.heading: An adventure moved by exercise
cards.text: Ring Fit Adventure is Nintendo's exercise role-playing game, released for Switch on 18 October 2019. The player advances through a fantasy adventure by performing physical activities, using a flexible Ring-Con held in the hands and a strap attached to the leg. Jogging and exercises move the journey forward, while battles turn selected movements into actions against enemies. The structure supplies a destination and a next challenge, connecting a session of repeated physical effort to the continuing progress of a character and a world.

cards.heading: A ring and a strap become the controller
cards.text: One Joy-Con fits into the Ring-Con and another into the Leg Strap. Motion sensing reads the player's movement, while the ring measures how it is pressed or pulled. The accessories make different exercises legible to the game and let those actions serve as controls. A battle becomes a sequence of chosen activities performed and measured, rather than commands selected without movement. The physical resistance of the ring supplies feedback that an ordinary button cannot, linking the action on screen to effort felt in the player's hands.

cards.heading: Build a routine around the next battle
cards.text: Alongside the adventure, guided routines and shorter minigames provide other ways to use the equipment. This variety allows a session to focus on a particular activity or continue the larger role-playing journey. Nintendo developed the project within its interest in games that support everyday activity, following the broader path established by Wii Fit. Ring Fit gives that aim an equipment-based identity of its own: the ring and strap remain simple objects, while the software turns their movement into a reason to return for another session.
